newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan May long-term prime seen set at 3.1% or 3.2%.
newsitem.headline: Japan May long-term prime seen set at 3.1% or 3.2%.

text.p: Japan's long-term prime lending rate for May is likely to be raised to 3.1 or 3.2 percent from 2.5 percent in April, bankers at long-term credit institutions said on Monday.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd is scheduled to announce its prime lending rate for May on Monday afternoon.
Bond analysts said it has taken longer than usual for the bank to decide on the new rate because the Ministry of Finance may have been wary of such a sharp rate increase.
If the rate is set at 3.1 or 3.2 percent, it would be the highest since August 1996, when it was 3.3 percent.
The prime rate, which is applied to loans of one year and longer to Japanese long-term credit banks' most creditworthy clients, is reviewed every month, reflecting market trends.
The prime rate was cut by 0.2 point to a record low 2.5 percent in December and has remained unchanged since then.

The prime rate is customarily set 0.9 percentage point above the coupon rate of IBJ's five-year debenture, which is issued monthly and is the benchmark in Japan's debenture market. Bank debentures are the long-term credit banks' major fund-raising tool.
IBJ's April 1.6 percent five-year debenture was bid-only at 2.35 percent on Monday morning after trading at 2.30 percent on Friday, traders said.
The other two long-term credit banks, the Long-Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd, are to announce their prime rates for May on Tuesday.
